title: Expectation of Finite Linear Combinations
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces, with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to $1$. For any finite set $s$, real coefficients $a_i$, and real-valued functions $F_i$ on the product outcome space, $\mathbb E_P[\sum_{i\in s}a_iF_i]=\sum_{i\in s}a_i\mathbb E_PF_i$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space
All coordinate weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$
Each $F_i$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, let $s$ be a finite index set, and let $a_j\in\mathbb R$ and $F_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P\sum_{j\in s}a_jF_j=\sum_{j\in s}a_j\mathbb E_PF_j$.
